summary: Sporting News rates each USMNT player after a 3-1 friendly defeat to Germany in Hartford. The U.S. was level at halftime after Christian Pulisic's goal and Ilkay Gundogan's equalizer, but defensive errors and a overrun midfield after the break let Germany take control. Pulisic (9), Matt Turner (8) and Tim Weah (8) were the standouts, while Chris Richards, Sergino Dest and Weston McKennie (all 4) were the weakest.
one_line: Player ratings for the USMNT's 3-1 loss to Germany in Hartford, with Pulisic and Weah excelling and the defense and midfield faltering.
key_facts: The USMNT lost 3-1 to Germany at Rentschler Field in Hartford; the match was level at halftime.
Christian Pulisic scored a first-half 'stunner' and was cancelled out by Ilkay Gundogan's goal, which came after Matt Turner initially saved a shot.
Christian Pulisic received the top rating of 9, completing 27 of 29 passes and creating two chances in addition to his goal; his corners were criticized as 'awful'.
Matt Turner was rated 8 for a host of excellent saves, but could have done better to marshal a scattered defensive line.
Tim Weah was rated 8 for electric pace, including scorching Robin Gosens on the wing in the first half; he played 66 minutes.
Gio Reyna was rated 7 in his first start back under Gregg Berhalter; he was only fit for 45 minutes as he returns from a leg injury and was replaced by Luca de la Torre (5) at halftime.
Chris Richards was rated 4: he completed all but one of 42 passes but was off the pace in his 65 minutes and poorly positioned.
On Germany's third goal, Richards stepped up to guard a free Niklas Fullkrug, leaving Leroy Sane free on goal because Tim Ream (rated 5) was unaware.

Sergino Dest was rated 4: lively going forward but he was non-existent as Leroy Sane scored the first goal and played Niklas Fullkrug onside on the second; he was filling in for Antonee Robinson at left-back.
Weston McKennie was rated 4 despite going 18/18 passing before the break and 28/30 overall, because his positioning was poor out of possession.
Yunus Musah was rated 6, nutmegging Florian Wirtz but whiffing on a slide on Germany's first goal.
Cameron Carter-Vickers (7) came on after recent hamstring troubles and had 22 touches, two dribbles completed and two clearances in 25 minutes.
Brenden Aaronson (7) was the most impactful substitute, while Ricardo Pepi (5) had just eight touches in 24 minutes.
Johnny Cardoso (6) and Kevin Paredes (5) came on in the 75th minute; the article questions why Cardoso or Lennard Maloney were not introduced at halftime.
